newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain returns outlaw communist's wig 20 years late.
newsitem.headline: Spain returns outlaw communist's wig 20 years late.

text.p: Spain returned on Tuesday a light-brown wig and lab coat worn as an ineffective disguise by ex-communist leader Santiago Carrillo when he was arrested 20 years ago.

The objects, symbols of Spain's transition to democracy after nearly 40 years of dictatorship, resurfaced in a police department and were handed back to the former secretary general of Spain's once-outlawed Communist Party in an official ceremony.

"This act is an important symbol, not only for Spain's transition 20 years ago, but for the transition today," a smiling Carrillo said as he received a box containing the wig, coat and fake facial hair from Rodolfo Martin Villa, the interior minister when he was arrested on December 22, 1976.
"It has been a bit surreal to get these back from the same interior minister who was considered the devil 20 years ago," he added.
After living in France in exile for 28 years, the balding Carrillo used the disguise to slip back across the border for almost a year before being arrested.
His imprisonment set off mass protests in the country as the population struggled to heal old wounds from the Civil War and reinstate free political expression.
The Communist Party was legalised three months later in an act considered by historians to be a turning point in Spain's transition to democracy.
